Hi, jl

You can try the following:

> # devtools::install_github("andrie/version.compare")
> library(version.compare)
> x <- RevoBenchmark(threads = c(1, 4), scale.factor = 0.2)
> plot(x)

This install the version.compare package from github and runs a simple benchmark using first a single thread, then 4 threads.  (Change threads=c(1, 4) to your desired number of cores you want to test on.)

You should get a plot similar to this:

Hi, Rich

If Hadley says that his package only works on 32-bit Windows, you'll need to use a 32-bit version of R to use his package.

RRO is only built (and supported) using 64-bit architecture.

Your options then are:
Use a 32-bit version of R - you may have to download R from CRAN
You may be able to build ggobi from source in a 64-bit architecture.
I hope this works out for you.

Andrie

messages.subject: MKL multithreaded library and mclapply do not play well together
messages.subject_clean: MKL multithreaded library and mclapply do not play well together
messages.body_plain:
After some testing, I have discovered that using mclapply on multiple cores with MKLthreads set to greater than 1 results in the threads sleeping and basically never finishing. Obviously, the temporary solution is to set MKLthreads to 1. But it would be nice if these functions worked together, because you cannot always guarantee that a package in R will not use mclapply while calling a MKL threaded math function, and there are situations where I would like to just use MKLthreads > 1 and not worry about it.

I am running Ubuntu 14.04 with RRO 3.2.1 and RStudio 0.99.486. I would upgrade to RRO 3.2.2, but it broke RStudio, so I downgraded.  I have an Intel 4-core processor with 2 threads per core.

Here is some code to test the problem:

library(parallel)
set.seed(1)
m <- 10000
n <- 2000
A <- matrix(runif (m*n),m,n)

setMKLthreads(1)
system.time(S <- svd (A,nu=0,nv=0))
# user  system elapsed
# 7.282   0.133   7.431

setMKLthreads(4)
system.time(S <- svd (A,nu=0,nv=0))
# user  system elapsed
# 16.584   0.347   5.377

setMKLthreads(1)
system.time(mclapply(X=list(A, A, A, A),
                     FUN=svd,
                     nu=0,
                     nv=0,
                     mc.cores=4))
# user  system elapsed
# 852.845  35.167  19.691

setMKLthreads(4)
system.time(mclapply(X=list(A, A, A, A),
                     FUN=svd,
                     nu=0,
                     nv=0,
                     mc.cores=1))
# user  system elapsed
# 66.333   1.245  21.573

setMKLthreads(4)
system.time(mclapply(X=list(A, A, A, A),
                     FUN=svd,
                     nu=0,
                     nv=0,
                     mc.cores=4))
# threads sleep; use 0% cpu and do not finish

messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I hope someone else will jump in on your mclapply issue, but the RStudio issue with RRO is likely fixable. Try the following:  As reported on Github <https://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/RRO/issues/241>, it may be related to the following: Line 4 in /usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib64/R/bin/R determines R_HOME_DIR based on readlink /proc/$$/fd/255. Since this command is implementation-dependent, it does not work the same way across each environment. Some users have had success by updating line 4 to use the absolute path to R such as:
R_HOME_DIR=/usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib64/R
R_HOME_DIR=/usr/lib64/RRO-3.2.2/R-3.2.2/lib/R
The actual path depends on your environment or distribution. Hope this helps.

Thanks,
Josée

There is a known problem with the MKL Installer on Windows when installing as a user who does not have administrative rights.
The MKL Installer needs administrative rights to successfully install on Windows systems.

Thank you,

messages.subject: Re: MKL multithreaded library and mclapply do not play well together
messages.subject_clean: MKL multithreaded library and mclapply do not play well together
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Michael

I plan to write in more detail on this topic in a blog post early next week, but I want to respond with some quick thoughts:

Most of the benefit of the MKL comes from fast vectorised math. The multithreaded computation adds a little bit to the performance, but in reality very little (see the performance benchmarks at https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/documents/rro/multithread/#mt-bench).
So, if you want to set and forget a setting, I suggest you use setMklthreads(1)
Parallel programming in R is hard and full of pitfalls.  Your problem with parallel math is just one of these.  See paragraph 2, "A word of caution" in the doParallel vignette (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/doParallel/vignettes/gettingstartedParallel.pdf) that points out other pitfalls.

 <https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/assets/img/bench1.d70e631d.png>

Regards

Andrie

> Parallel programming in R is hard and full of pitfalls.  Your problem with parallel math is just one of these.  See paragraph 2, "A word of caution" in the doParallel vignette (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/doParallel/vignettes/gettingstartedParallel.pdf) that points out other pitfalls.
>
>  <https://mran.revolutionanalytics.com/assets/img/bench1.d70e631d.png>
>
>
> Regards
>
>
> Andrie
>
>
> On Monday, October 12, 2015 at 10:43:28 PM UTC+1, Michael wrote:
> > After some testing, I have discovered that using mclapply on multiple cores with MKLthreads set to greater than 1 results in the threads sleeping and basically never finishing. Obviously, the temporary solution is to set MKLthreads to 1. But it would be nice if these functions worked together, because you cannot always guarantee that a package in R will not use mclapply while calling a MKL threaded math function, and there are situations where I would like to just use MKLthreads > 1 and not worry about it.
> >
> > I am running Ubuntu 14.04 with RRO 3.2.1 and RStudio 0.99.486. I would upgrade to RRO 3.2.2, but it broke RStudio, so I downgraded.  I have an Intel 4-core processor with 2 threads per core.
> >
> > Here is some code to test the problem:
> >
> > library(parallel)
> > set.seed(1)
> > m <- 10000
> > n <- 2000
> > A <- matrix(runif (m*n),m,n)
> >
> >
> > setMKLthreads(1)
> > system.time(S <- svd (A,nu=0,nv=0))
> > # user  system elapsed
> > # 7.282   0.133   7.431
> >
> >
> > setMKLthreads(4)
> > system.time(S <- svd (A,nu=0,nv=0))
> > # user  system elapsed
> > # 16.584   0.347   5.377
> >
> >
> > setMKLthreads(1)
> > system.time(mclapply(X=list(A, A, A, A),
> >                      FUN=svd,
> >                      nu=0,
> >                      nv=0,
> >                      mc.cores=4))
> > # user  system elapsed
> > # 852.845  35.167  19.691
> >
> >
> > setMKLthreads(4)
> > system.time(mclapply(X=list(A, A, A, A),
> >                      FUN=svd,
> >                      nu=0,
> >                      nv=0,
> >                      mc.cores=1))
> > # user  system elapsed
> > # 66.333   1.245  21.573
> >
> >
> > setMKLthreads(4)
> > system.time(mclapply(X=list(A, A, A, A),
> >                      FUN=svd,
> >                      nu=0,
> >                      nv=0,
> >                      mc.cores=4))
> > # threads sleep; use 0% cpu and do not finish
> >
